item.title: Swiss Bank Sygnum Says Bitcoin Could Reach New High Near $128,000
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Swiss Bank Sygnum Says Bitcoin Could Reach New High Near $128,000 Sygnum Bank estimates that bitcoin could reach a new all-time high near $128,000. The Swiss digital asset bank laid out the scenario in its 2027 Sygnal outlook on Thursday, alongside a call that bitcoin and ether will both set new highs while the broader market stays narrow. The report also frames the current downturn as the shallowest bear market for bitcoin to date. Sygnum puts the drawdown at around 54%, compared with declines of more than 70% in previous cycles, and says digital assets enter 2027 with lower structural volatility and stronger fundamentals. The outlook arrives as bitcoin trades near $63,000 after six straight weekly losses and a drop below its 200-week moving average. Sygnum’s case is that the market has changed since earlier cycles, not that the slide is over. Sygnum describes a more mature market. Volatility is increasingly driven by broader dollar liquidity and market structure, it said, and institutions have added new channels through ETFs, leveraged trading and crypto-backed credit. By the end of October, stablecoin supply stood near $298 billion and tokenized real-world assets exceeded $39 billion. JUST IN: Switzerland's Sygnum Bank estimates that Bitcoin could hit a new high of $128,000. Its 2027 outlook also calls this Bitcoin's "shallowest bear market yet". pic.twitter.com/KWyFALBAR8 — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 19, 2026 How bitcoin gets to $128,000 The estimate rests on a rotation out of technology stocks. Digital assets are worth about 6% of the Nasdaq’s market value, and Sygnum calculates that if 0.75% of Nasdaq value, roughly $360 billion, moved into crypto, total market capitalization could rise by more than 60%. In that scenario, bitcoin would reach a new high near $128,000. The report does not put a date on it and describes the figure as an estimate built on Sygnum’s own calculations, not a price target. It also notes that a sell-off in AI stocks could spill into crypto. Currently, Anthropic’s record $81 billion IPO is set to open about 25% to 30% above its $83 offering price, which has lifted AI and chip stocks, but worries about higher interest rates have pulled the Nasdaq back from an early 2% gain to about 0.3%. Bitcoin moves into the reserve bucket Behind the price call is a shift in how institutions treat bitcoin. Sygnum predicts it will move out of the tactical sleeve of portfolios and into the “strategic reserve bucket,” competing with gold for capital that wants protection against currency debasement. BlackRock, Morgan Stanley and Bank of America each recommend allocations of 1% to 4%. The report says 2027 should reward selection over broad market exposure. Sygnum expects adoption to concentrate in stablecoins, tokenized assets, bitcoin as an institutional macro asset and tokens with proven usage, and it believes investors will be rewarded for choosing assets with real usage and revenue. item.title: Huge New Nvidia Bug Is Ruining Gaming Hardware, Users Say
item.description: Nvidia is in rough shape. As the hardware company scrambles to replace its CEO and co-founder, Jensen Huang , after a series of scandals, it seems the needs of lowly gamers aren’t high on the priority list. Earlier this year, the company ran into controversy over its ugly generative AI-fueled DLSS 5 technology . If you need more evidence that Nvidia is focused on cranking out chips for generative AI rather than supporting its gaming hardware, the company has failed to fix a bug reportedly capable of damaging users’ PCs by writing excessive amounts of data to solid-state drives (SSDs).

item.title: Court restrains Jimmy Odukoya from parading as Fountain of Life senior pastor
item.description: The Lagos State High Court has restrained Jimmy Odukoya from parading himself as the Senior Pastor and spiritual head of the Fountain of Life Church, Lagos. Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin according to TheCable, granted the order on Wednesday following a suit instituted by the incorporated trustees of the church. The trustees had sought a pre-emptive order of injunction restraining Odukoya from presenting himself as the church’s Senior Pastor and interfering with its activities, governance and other affairs. They argued that Odukoya had ceased to hold the position following the appointment of a successor by the late founder and Senior Pastor of the church, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya. In the suit, the trustees sought an order restraining Odukoya, whether acting personally or through proxies, from interfering with, disrupting, meddling with or obstructing the activities and governance of the church pending compliance with the High Court of Lagos State (Expeditious Disposal of Civil Cases) Practice Directions No. 2 of 2019 on pre-action protocol. Granting the application, Justice Adewunmi-Oshin ruled: “Leave is hereby granted to the Applicant to commence this action under the Pre-Action Protocol pursuant to Paragraph 4 of the High Court of Lagos State (Expeditious Disposal of Civil Cases) Practice Direction No. 2 of 2019.” The order followed the trustees’ application for judicial intervention in the leadership and administration of the church. The post Court restrains Jimmy Odukoya from parading as Fountain of Life senior pastor appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Atiku demands scrutiny of INEC’s AI system for processing election results
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, to open its proposed artificial intelligence system for processing election results to independent audit ahead of the 2027 general elections. Atiku wants the commission to disclose how the technology works, who developed it and what safeguards are in place to prevent valid polling unit results from being flagged, delayed or excluded during electronic processing. In a statement by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said he had petitioned the INEC Chairman on behalf of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, and allied democratic stakeholders, demanding algorithmic transparency, independent scrutiny and clear rules for human oversight. The petition follows INEC’s announced integration of artificial intelligence and intelligent document processing into the process linking its Data Verification and Authentication System, DIVAS, with the INEC Result Viewing portal, IReV. Warning against placing public confidence in an opaque technology, Atiku said: “INEC cannot ask Nigerians to trust a system whose rules they are forbidden to see. If an algorithm can flag a polling unit result sheet, the public deserves to know what triggers that flag, who set the threshold, who can change it and what happens to the result afterward.” He demanded publication of the system’s technical and operational framework, including its training data sources, criteria for flagging discrepancies and the identities of its developers and third-party vendors. He also wants independent cybersecurity experts, political party technology representatives and civil society technologists to have access to the source code, training data and decision logs for a comprehensive audit before the nationwide mock accreditation scheduled for November 28, 2026. On the legal status of polling unit results, Atiku insisted that the physical Form EC8A, completed and signed at the polling unit, must remain the primary evidence of what transpired there, warning against allowing an algorithmic assessment to override it. “The polling unit result sheet, Form EC8A, records what happened where the people voted. INEC must publicly reaffirm the legal status of the physical form completed and signed at the polling unit, and explain how it will resolve any conflict between that document and an AI assessment. “A machine’s verdict cannot be allowed to quietly displace the evidence witnessed by voters and party agents,” he said. Atiku also demanded a transparent procedure for reviewing flagged result sheets, including the officials responsible for such reviews, documentation of decisions, notification of political parties and mechanisms for promptly challenging errors. He proposed real-time monitoring access for political parties through a dedicated dashboard or observer interface to enable them to identify unusual patterns of flagging, delays or blocked uploads

item.title: Amazon’s last-gen Kindle Paperwhite hasn’t been this cheap since June
item.description: alt: Amazon’s last-gen Kindle Paperwhite is just $10 more than the base model alt: The last-gen Kindle Paperwhite for $130 is a stellar Black Friday deal Amazon debuted its latest Kindle Paperwhite in October, which is now available for $199.99 and replaces the outgoing 2024 model. However, given the minimal improvements on the new model — it’s a little thinner and opens books faster — the last-gen Paperwhite is still one of the best e-readers you can buy. And now, the latter is down to $129.99 ($70 off), nearly its lowest price ever, at Amazon , Best Buy , and Target . Some important pricing context: The waterproof e-reader held steady at $159.99 until late August, when its price rose 25 percent due to rising component costs ( many other Amazon tech products got more expensive, too). Even if the price hike never happened, though, this would still be a nice discount. Kindle Paperwhite (2024) Where to Buy: $199.99 $129.99 at Amazon (with ads) $199.99 $129.99 at Best Buy (with ads) $199.99 $129.99 at Amazon (with ads) The $129.99 Paperwhite includes 16GB of storage and features lockscreen ads (it costs $20 extra to opt out at checkout), just like the newer version. It also packs a sharp 300ppi display with adjustable color temperature and USB-C charging. If you want more features — including twice the storage, zero ads, wireless charging, and an auto-adjusting front light — opt instead for the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition while it’s down to $179.99 (also $70 off), which is just $10 shy of its best price to date. For the sake of being comprehensive, the last-gen base Kindle is going for $119.99 ($30 off) at Amazon ahead of Black Friday. While the standard Kindle has improved with each new iteration, it’s tough to recommend when the vastly superior Paperwhite is on sale for just $10 more. That 10 bucks gets you so much: waterproofing, better battery life, faster page-turning speeds, and a higher pixel density screen that’s slightly larger (7 inches vs. 6 inches). item.title: Anambra home to political icons like Zik, Ekwueme, Soludo – Shettima
item.description: By Nwabueze Okonkwo ONITSHA – Vice-President Kashim Shettima has described Anambra State as a home of accomplished political leaders, citing Nigeria’s first President, Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe; former Vice-President, Dr. Alex Ekwueme; and the incumbent governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo. Shettima made the observation on Thursday at a joint mega rally organised by the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) and the All Progressives Congress (APC) under the banner of Progressives Working Together. The Vice-President, who represented President Bola Tinubu at the rally, said he was not surprised that Soludo had embraced what he described as the visionary politics of national unity associated with Azikiwe and Ekwueme. He commended the governor for what he described as his courage and political approach in the current political dispensation. Shettima also assured Nigerians, particularly residents of Anambra State, that Tinubu’s administration would reposition the country if given another term in 2027. In his remarks, Soludo said APGA and APC had unanimously endorsed Tinubu for a second term in office. As part of the alliance, the governor handed over the APGA flag to the APC, describing the move as a demonstration of the parties’ commitment to working together. Soludo further disclosed that elected APGA members in the state and National Assemblies would work with their APC counterparts in their respective legislative caucuses. He said the arrangement was aimed at promoting cooperation, national unity and the indivisibility of Nigeria. item.title: Tinubu doesn’t need to rig 2027 election, Soludo says
item.description: Anambra State Governor, Chukwuma Soludo, has declared that President Bola Tinubu does not need to rig the 2027 presidential election to secure re-election, expressing confidence that the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) would win the contest. Soludo made the declaration on Thursday while speaking at a presidential campaign rally at Alex Ekwueme Square, Awka, where he argued that the APC had a stronger nationwide political presence than its opponents. “This election, to the best of our knowledge, is already won and lost. The president doesn’t need to rig any election. President Tinubu doesn’t need to rig any election,” he said. Explaining his position, the governor said the APC presidential ticket was facing opposition candidates whose political influence, according to him, was limited to certain parts of the country. “All over the country today, in every state of Nigeria, it is President Tinubu and Shettima ticket versus one other party. Whereas you have some other candidates who are strong in some parts of the country but don’t exist in others. “If you then take the totality of it all, do the arithmetic in your mind, this election is literally over,” Soludo said. He also attributed his confidence to the performance of the Tinubu administration, arguing that the President and Vice-President Kashim Shettima deserved another term based on their record in office. “President Tinubu, Shettima, they’re doing very well. They will win because they have done well,” he said. The governor further argued that the APC had presented a stronger policy agenda than its opponents, claiming that no credible alternative had emerged ahead of the election. “And let me put it on record, in terms of the agenda that they are pursuing, no candidate before 2023 presented a better manifesto, better agenda for Nigeria. “And so far, less than two months to go, no candidate has presented a credible alternative. The Tinubu-Shettima ticket presidency is on course,” he said. Soludo also defended the Federal Government’s handling of the economy and security, claiming that there was a consensus among people familiar with the economy, both locally and internationally, that the administration was moving in the right direction. He cited the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), which provides financial support to eligible students, as one of the initiatives through which the administration was addressing the needs of Nigerians. item.title: Kwara South: APC candidate Adewoye confident of victory
item.description: By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin The All Progressives Congress (APC) senatorial candidate for Kwara South in the 2027 general election, Prince Olalekan Adewoye, has expressed confidence in his ability to represent the people of the district effectively, saying his business experience and grassroots interventions have prepared him for public service. Adewoye said his conviction was anchored on more than three decades of experience in business, philanthropic activities and commitment to grassroots development. Speaking in an interview with journalists, the industrialist said he was passionate about translating his private-sector experience into public service, despite not having previously held an elective position or served as a political appointee. Addressing concerns about his lack of political experience and the challenge posed by established opposition politicians, Adewoye said he was confident of earning the support of voters. “I am convinced of my capacity and believe I have what it takes to represent the people effectively,” he said. He argued that voters should assess candidates based on their records, capacity and acceptability rather than previous political positions alone. According to him, his years in business have equipped him with the ability to manage people from different backgrounds, create value and deploy resources efficiently. He said these skills would be useful in legislative representation, particularly in ensuring that public resources and government programmes deliver tangible benefits to constituents. Adewoye disclosed that before joining the senatorial race, he had been involved in philanthropic activities through a foundation established to address some of the social and economic challenges facing residents of Kwara South. He identified healthcare, education and support for small businesses as critical areas requiring attention in the district. He said the foundation had provided equipment to individuals seeking to establish or expand businesses, supported healthcare interventions, including health insurance for elderly people, and assisted artisans and other vulnerable groups. According to him, the interventions were designed to promote self-reliance and economic independence rather than encourage beneficiaries to depend on periodic handouts. “We should not simply tell young people to look for jobs. We must help them acquire the skills, resources and support they need to create value,” he said. The APC candidate said his proposed representation would prioritise expanding economic opportunities for young people, traders, artisans and small business operators. He also disclosed plans to establish a trust fund to bring together individuals and organisations willing to support entrepreneurs and other deserving residents of Kwara South. item.title: NAND prices tipped to fall as Chinese cloud giants cut SSD orders
item.description: NAND flash prices could start falling next year as Chinese cloud operators cut enterprise SSD orders, helping push the market toward oversupply. Taiwan-based market intelligence firm TrendForce says Chinese cloud service providers are grappling with GPU shortages, high inventories, and fierce competition over AI token pricing. As a result, they have reduced their total enterprise SSD orders for 2027 by a substantial amount. Although TrendForce doesn't specify any figures, it says the cutbacks in China are large enough to outweigh the additional demand coming from US-based cloud operators. But don't get too excited: TrendForce forecasts overall NAND flash contract prices falling by 0-5 percent quarter on quarter in early 2027, with all product categories entering a downturn from the second quarter. Falling orders are only half the story. Manufacturers are also increasing output, while weaker consumer electronics sales could further depress demand. Strong demand for high-performance storage in the US continues to drive manufacturers to expand capacity and upgrade to newer process technologies. At the same time, the rising adoption of quad-level cell (QLC) technology and increasing number of layers in the NAND chips will further boost bit output, TrendForce observes. Some suppliers may go slower on their expansion plans in response to sluggish consumer demand, but the firm still expects global NAND flash output, measured in storage capacity, to grow by 25 to 30 percent in 2027. US restrictions on access to advanced AI chips could put Chinese cloud operators under further pressure. The US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has introduced new restrictions on sales of GPUs, and on remote access to them via the cloud. The new restrictions " set everyone back in China ," as The Register reported. TrendForce adds the caveat to its forecast that its market outlook depends on factors such as the pace of inventory reduction among Chinese CSPs, further changes to the restrictions on overseas GPU procurement, and whether device makers continue reducing storage capacities in 2028. Sadly, cheaper NAND wouldn't resolve the separate squeeze on DRAM supplies. The situation, caused by memory makers opting to produce high-margin products for the AI market rather than mainstream chips, has already increased prices of PCs in Europe by double-digit percentages, leading to a fall in shipments as buyers balk at the cost. ®

item.title: Sanwo-Olu gives LASUED best graduate N5m, job
item.description: By Elizabeth Osayande Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has rewarded the overall best graduating student of the Lagos State University of Education (LASUED), Blessed Mercy Olawunmi, with N5 million and automatic employment. The award was announced on Thursday, November 19, during the institution’s maiden convocation ceremony held at its Oto/Ijanikin campus. Olawunmi, of the Department of Home Economics, College of Vocational and Entrepreneurship Education, emerged top of the pioneering graduating class of 2,486 students, including 84 first-class graduates, with a Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) of 4.98. Sanwo-Olu also announced a cash reward of N2.5 million each for the best graduating students from the university’s seven colleges. Apart from the governor’s award, Olawunmi received N250,000 and a commemorative plaque from the university, while Oto-Awori Local Government presented her with N1 million. The council chairman, Kareem Azeez Abiodun, also announced a reward of N500,000 each for the other best graduating students from the colleges. Speaking at the ceremony, the Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Bidemi Bilkis Lafiaji-Okuneye, thanked Sanwo-Olu for assenting to the law establishing the university in 2022. She also commended the Governing Council, staff, students and other stakeholders for their contributions towards making the institution a source of pride. However, she appealed to the governor to intervene in four areas requiring urgent attention: construction of a podcast and photojournalism studio, reconstruction of the perimeter fence, reclamation of swampy land at the main campus and completion of the 750-seat auditoriums at the Epe and Ijanikin campuses. The Vice-Chancellor disclosed that more than 60 per cent of the main campus land was swampy, leaving the institution with limited space for expansion. She said the university currently occupied only the dry portions of the land and was becoming increasingly cramped, adding that reclamation would provide room for future development. She noted that a female hostel being constructed by the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) was already located on the site. “Your Excellency, sir, these four appeals are strategic investments rather than isolated requests. A studio will enrich what we teach. Secure fencing will protect people who teach — our land. Reclaimed land will create room for all that we still hope to build. An auditorium will provide a gathering space in which scholarship, professional development, and public engagement can flourish,” she said. Lafiaji-Okuneye also appreciated the Governing Council for its guidance and oversight, the Ministry of Tertiary Education for facilitating the university’s requests to the governor, and staff for sustaining the institution through its transition. item.title: Don't miss Saturn shine close to the moon on Nov. 20
item.description: null The moon shines close to the ringed giant Saturn after sunset on Nov. 20, presenting a spectacular naked-eye display as the stars of the Great Square of Pegasus twinkle nearby. Saturn's steady light will appear a little over 5 degrees from the 82%-lit moon in the southeastern sky after the sun dips below the horizon for viewers in the U.S. — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length. Moonlight will hide fainter stars from view, though you should be able to spot Algenib, Markab, Alpheratz and Scheat arrayed in a diamond formation above the lunar disk, marking out the asterism of the Great Square of Pegasus in the November sky. The moon will present a spectacular target through the eyepiece of a 6-inch telescope, as the terminator line separating night from day creeps ever closer to its western edge. It's a great time to explore the 110 km-wide Gassendi Crater on the edge of Mare Humorum as its eastern rim and central peaks throw intense shadows across its interior. Gassendi Crater is a fascinating target for telescope observation during the moon's waxing gibbous phase. (Image credit: Created by Anthony Wood in Canva. Inset: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio.) Slewing your telescope over to Saturn will reveal details and subtle variations in the cloud surface of the gas giant , along with its iconic ring system, which is gradually becoming more visible following its ring plane crossing in March 2025. Depending on viewing conditions, you may also notice a shoal of bright, star-like points of light surrounding Saturn's disk, which represent the large moons Titan , Dione , Tethys , Rhea and Iapetus . Interested in seeing the planets of the solar system up close for yourself? Then be sure to check out our picks of the best telescopes available in 2026 , including the Celestron NexStar 8SE , which we rate as the best motorized scope out there. Editor's Note: If you would like to share your planetary astrophotography with Space.com's readers, then please send your photo(s), comments, and your name and location to spacephotos@space.com.

item.title: 2027: Tinubu Doesn’t Need To Rig Any Election, He’ll Win Because He’s Done Well — Soludo
item.description: Anambra State Governor, Charles Soludo, has declared that President Bola Tinubu does not need to manipulate the 2027 presidential election to secure re-election, insisting that his performance in office will earn him victory. Soludo said the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential ticket of Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima was already in a strong position ahead of the election, arguing that no opposition candidate had presented a credible alternative to the ruling party. The governor spoke on Thursday at a 2027 presidential campaign rally in Anambra State attended by Shettima, Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council Abdul’aziz Yari, former Anambra State governor Chris Ngige and Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma, among other party chieftains. “To our people, this election, to the best of our knowledge, is already won and lost. The President doesn’t need to rig the election. President Tinubu doesn’t need to rig the election “All over the country today, in every state of Nigeria, it is President Tinubu and Shetima’s ticket versus one other party. Whereas you have some other candidates who are strong in some parts of the country but don’t exist in others. “If you then take the totality of it all, do the arithmetic. This election is literally over. President Tinubu and Shettima, they are doing very well. They will win because they have done well,” he added. ﻿ Soludo also praised the Tinubu administration’s economic policies, security efforts and social intervention programmes, describing its agenda as superior to those presented by previous presidential candidates. “We know that there is still work to be done. And that work to be done means moving now from stability, having rescued the economy from total collapse, now moving into the next phase of shared prosperity. But let’s not kid ourselves. You don’t change a winning team. The Tinubu-Shetima ticket is the winning team,” the governor said. 2027 Presidential Election COMBO: Peter Obi, Atiku Abubakar, Bola Tinubu and Omoyele Sowore The 2027 presidential election, which is less than 60 days away, is expected to feature several prominent political figures, including Tinubu of the APC, Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Peter Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), and Omoyele Sowore of the African Action Congress (AAC). Tinubu, who is seeking a second four-year term, won the 2023 presidential election with 8,794,726 votes. Atiku finished second with 6,984,520 votes, while Obi came third with 6,101,533 votes. Following the 2023 election, both Atiku and Obi challenged Tinubu’s victory, citing alleged electoral irregularities, delays in uploading results, and problems with the Independent National Electoral Commission’s (INEC) result transmission portal. item.title: 2027: APGA adopts Tinubu, says, you don’t change a winning team
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Grand Alliance APGA has presented its flag to President Bola Tinubu as its presidential candidate at the All Progressives Congress APC campaign rally in Awka, Anambra State. APC National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, announced the alliance at the rally held at Alex Ekwueme Square on Thursday. “The chairman of PDP is not here, but he is well in his spirit. The chairman of Accord is here. We are four in one. Four political parties supporting one candidate. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said. Yilwatda then invited Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, to present the APGA flag, with Vice President Kashim Shettima receiving it on Tinubu’s behalf. Soludo said the handover made the rally unlike any other. He said it was the first time APGA was presenting its flag to the Tinubu/Shettima ticket as its presidential candidate. He also reminded the crowd that Anambra was where the ticket did worst in 2023. According to him, it recorded 5,111 votes, or 0.8 per cent. “Ndi Anambra, are we going to do far better than 2023? We will not be there again,” he said. The governor said Ndigbo would lose from another round of political isolation. “Let us make this campaign a conversation, not an argument among ourselves. In a democracy, what leverage do we have other than our votes and having alliance with the rest of the country?There is work to be done, but you don’t change a winning team”, he said. Soludo said power would move to the North in 2031 and that the South should first complete its eight years. He also said the contest was already decided. “This election, to the best of my knowledge, is already won and lost. No candidate before 2023 presented a better manifesto, better agenda for Nigeria. And so far, less than two months to go, no candidate has presented a credible alternative,” he said. Yilwatda said the President had shown confidence in the Southeast by giving its sons key roles. He named the Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, who he said is constructimg good roads. He said even the opposition used those roads. “Even Peter Obi is using our roads. Atiku is using our roads. Those roads are constructed by your son, Umahi,” he said. Yilwatda described Tinubu as the most experienced and formidable of the candidates, pointing to his record as Lagos State governor and at the centre. He said the President had stabilised the economy and fixed roads, power and education. The Director General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Abdul’aziz Yari, urged Ndigbo to turn their economic weight into political influence. He cited the late President Muhammadu Buhari as proof that regional support alone does not win the presidency. “Buhari used to have 12 states in Northern Nigeria. At any point in time, he would get those 12 states. But that did not make him become President of Nigeria. But when he got the South-West, he made it. Buhari lost in 2003, 2007 and 2011 before winning in 2015, when he had a frien

item.title: Man accused of AI-assisted exam cheating found dead in Seoul
item.description: A South Korean man suspected of using artificial intelligence (AI) to obtain a perfect score in the country’s law school entrance examination has been found dead at a motel in Seoul. Lee Jin-woo was discovered at a motel in Cheonho-dong, Gangdong District, eastern Seoul, at about 1:12 p.m. on Thursday, emergency authorities said. According to Yonhap News TV, a note was also found at the scene, reportedly indicating that Lee was physically and mentally exhausted. However, the note reportedly contained no admission of cheating or explanation of the allegations against him. Authorities said they would examine the scene to establish the circumstances surrounding his death. Lee had attracted public attention over allegations that he used AI to cheat in the Legal Education Eligibility Test (LEET), the examination required for admission into law schools in South Korea. In an attempt to dispel the suspicions, he had announced plans to answer questions from the Korean language section of the 2027 College Scholastic Ability Test in real time on Thursday morning. However, he failed to appear at the designated venue by 8:40 a.m., when the examination began. Police launched a search after receiving a report at about 8:42 a.m. expressing concern over his whereabouts. According to the police, Lee left his home on Wednesday and travelled to a lodging facility in Gwangjin District, eastern Seoul, before leaving on Thursday morning. He reportedly took a taxi towards Songpa District, southern Seoul, between 8 a.m. and 9 a.m., before heading to Gangdong District, where his body was later discovered. Lee had previously gained attention after revealing that he had scored between the sixth and eighth tiers in previous college entrance examinations, which use a nine-tier grading system, with higher numbers representing lower scores. He said he later developed a better understanding of studying and reading comprehension, eventually gaining admission into Korea University’s Department of Political Science and International Relations in 2024 and Seoul National University’s School of Dentistry in 2026. He also reportedly achieved a perfect score in the LEET while attending Seoul National University. However, his academic achievements came under scrutiny following allegations of AI-assisted cheating in a national tax accountant certification examination. Questions were subsequently raised over whether he had also used AI to cheat in the LEET and the college entrance examinations for the 2024 and 2026 academic years. The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency said on Wednesday that it had assigned a criminal complaint against Lee, bordering on allegations of obstruction of business, obstruction of official duties and fraud, to its Provincial Special Detective Corps. Following his death, police are expected to close the case without prosecution, as criminal proceedings cannot continue against a deceased suspect. item.title: Fountain of Life Church postpones 2026 Thanksgiving service
item.description: The Fountain of Life Church has postponed its 2026 Thanksgiving service, earlier scheduled for Sunday, November 22, amid an ongoing leadership crisis involving Senior Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and members of its Board of Trustees. The Lagos-based church announced the postponement in a notice shared on its official social media platforms on Thursday, November 19. The notice read, “Please be informed that our Thanksgiving 2026 Service, previously scheduled for Sunday, November 22, has been postponed. A new date will be communicated in due course.” The church did not give any reason for the decision or indicate when the service would be rescheduled. The development comes amid a leadership dispute following an announcement by some members of the Board of Trustees withdrawing recognition of Odukoya as the church’s senior pastor with immediate effect. The trustees reportedly based their decision on a review of the church’s constitution and a December 2021 video recording in which the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, outlined succession arrangements that identified another individual as his preferred successor, while assigning Jimmy Odukoya administrative and youth church responsibilities. They also cited governance concerns and issues surrounding Odukoya’s recent remarriage. However, Odukoya and representatives of the church rejected the announcement, describing it as constitutionally invalid and not a decision properly taken by the Board of Trustees. They maintained that he remains the duly appointed senior pastor and chairman of the board, following his unanimous approval for the positions in September 2023 after his father’s death. The trustees subsequently reaffirmed their position and appointed Pastor Rotimi Okpaise to provide interim spiritual and administrative leadership pending further consultations. The crisis has also extended to the control of the church’s official social media accounts, with both sides reportedly disputing authority over the platforms. Odukoya was notably absent from the church’s midweek service on Thursday as the leadership dispute continued. The Thanksgiving service had attracted attention amid the unfolding crisis, with the postponement adding another development to the dispute over the church’s leadership and administration. The post Fountain of Life Church postpones 2026 Thanksgiving service appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: CLARITY Act Likely Dead Until 2027, Top Crypto Lawmakers Warn
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine CLARITY Act Likely Dead Until 2027, Top Crypto Lawmakers Warn House Financial Services Committee Chairman French Hill said the CLARITY Act is unlikely to pass before the year ends, leaving the crypto market structure bill to a new Congress that Democrats will control. Hill spoke Thursday at the Capitol Crypto Forum in Washington. “We never give up hope in a lame duck, but it is lame, and therefore the chances are not high,” the Arkansas Republican said . He added that he plans to make market structure legislation his pitch in the next Congress, which begins in January. “I regret that it was not something we could get done effectively in this Congress,” Hill said. He said 78 Democrats voted for the CLARITY Act in the House and that he expects that support to continue in the new Congress. Hill also called it encouraging that Rep. Maxine Waters, the committee’s top Democrat, circulated a memo to House Democrats naming digital asset market structure as a topic she intends to work on if she becomes chair. Senate floor time is running out Sen. Bernie Moreno, the lead sponsor of the CLARITY Act in the Senate, told the same forum there is “no scenario” in which crypto legislation passes the chamber during the lame-duck session. Funding the government, the National Defense Authorization Act and the farm bill will take priority, according to The Hill, and the session is set to end in less than a month. The Senate blocked the CLARITY Act on Sept. 15, voting 49-50 on a procedural motion that needed 60 votes. All Democrats and four Republicans opposed it, CBS News reported. Sen. Thom Tillis entered a motion to reconsider, which keeps the option of another vote alive, but the bill dies when this Congress ends Jan. 3 unless the lame-duck session revives it. The House passed the legislation 294-134 in July 2025. President Donald Trump urged lawmakers in August to send it to his desk, but Democrats objected that its ethics provisions did not go far enough to address his potential conflicts of interest in crypto, and regulators have since moved ahead on their own, including an SEC exemption for tokenized stocks. Democrats prepare to take over The industry is now scrambling to repair its relationship with Democrats, Politico reported Thursday. The industry spent $55 million trying to defeat Sen.-elect Sherrod Brown of Ohio, who won his seat back, and Democrats are set to retake both the House and Senate in January. Sen. Ruben Gallego, a crypto-friendly Arizona Democrat who spent months negotiating the Senate bill, gave Politico’s Jasper Goodman a blunt assessment of the industry’s political prospects. “They’re f***ed,” Gallego said, according to a post from journalist Eleanor Terrett. Terrett has reported that House Democrats are discussing turning Waters’ Crypto Investor and Consumer Bill of Rights into their own market structure bill. item.title: Road crashes fall 13.8%, deaths drop to 941 in Q3 2026 — FRSC
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) has reported a 13.8 per cent reduction in road traffic crashes across Nigeria in the third quarter of 2026, with fatalities dropping from 1,077 in the corresponding period of 2025 to 941. The Corps also recorded a decline in the number of people injured, from 6,856 to 5,864, representing a 14.5 per cent reduction. The figures were disclosed in a statement on Thursday by the Corps Public Education Officer, Osondu Ohaeri, following the end-of-year strategy session with commanding officers at the FRSC headquarters in Abuja. According to the statement, 2,098 road traffic crashes were recorded between July and September 2026, compared with 2,434 in the corresponding period of 2025. The reduction of 336 crashes exceeded the Corps’ 10 per cent reduction target. Similarly, the number of people injured dropped by 992, while fatalities declined by 136, representing a 12.6 per cent reduction. The statement said, “A comparative assessment of the two periods shows that road traffic crashes declined from 2,434 in Q3 2025 to 2,098 in Q3 2026, representing 336 fewer crashes. “Road traffic injuries also dropped significantly from 6,856 to 5,864, a reduction of 992, while recorded fatalities decreased from 1,077 to 941, representing 136 fewer deaths.” The Corps attributed the improvement to enhanced patrol operations, crash prevention measures, public education and enforcement of traffic laws. Ahead of the 2026 festive season, the Corps Marshal, Shehu Mohammed, directed commanding officers nationwide to intensify patrol operations along high-risk routes, improve traffic management and strengthen collaboration with other security and emergency response agencies. He also ordered the strategic deployment of ambulances, rescue teams and tow trucks, while directing commands to sustain public awareness campaigns on safe driving. “As the nation approaches the 2026 festive season, the Corps Marshal has directed Commanding Officers across the country to translate the gains recorded into more effective highway operations, with particular attention to strategic patrol deployment along high-risk corridors, improved traffic management, stronger collaboration with sister agencies, strategic positioning of ambulances, rescue teams and tow trucks, and sustained public enlightenment,” the statement added. Mohammed also urged commanding officers to strengthen supervision, prioritise personnel welfare and enforce discipline, warning that the Corps would maintain zero tolerance for extortion, negligence and abuse of authority. In his remarks, the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, George Akume, said the figures reflected progress made under the reforms introduced by the Corps Marshal, particularly the increased emphasis on technology and operational intelligence. item.title: Surprising No One, GTA 6's Comedy Is All Over the Place
item.description: More than being deviously fun crime sandboxes, every Grand Theft Auto game also acts as a snapshot of American culture at the time of its release. These games have never pulled any punches, taking swings at everything from the paparazzi to politics to the most innocuous corners of pop culture. GTA 6 was sure to take the same shots, but at a time when the targets are moving faster than ever. Could a game that has been in the works for more than a decade possibly have humor that felt up to date? Would it be careful to punch up rather than turn the country’s most vulnerable people into punchlines? And would it have the stones to take on President Donald Trump, a man who has dominated America’s political culture throughout the game’s entire development cycle?

item.title: ‎2027: APGA endorses Tinubu
item.description: ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA — Ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election, the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) on Thursday adopted President Bola Tinubu as its presidential candidate and handed him the party’s flag. ‎ ‎Governor Charles Soludo and the party’s national chairman handed the flag to President Tinubu at an All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign event in Awka, Anambra State. ‎ ‎Prof. Soludo said, “We resolved, in the spirit of one Nigeria, progressivism, cooperative federalism, unity and the progress of our indivisible, united Nigeria, to hand our flag to Prese ent Tinubu.” ‎ ‎He said all APGA members would canvass votes for President Tinubu. ‎He advocated political engagement and bridge-building rather than what he described as isolationism, saying this approach would ensure regional prosperity. ‎ ‎Soludo said Ndigbo should adopt a political strategy that rejects political isolation and ethnic intolerance, noting that such attitudes limit political leverage and risk wasting productive years through internal conflict. ‎ ‎He encouraged building bridges towards a united nation where all citizens could thrive, regardless of their location or ethnicity. He also asserted that the 2027 election was effectively decided in favour of the Tinubu/Shettima ticket. ‎ ‎He claimed that no other presidential candidate had presented a credible alternative or a superior manifesto. He added that there was significant consensus on the administration’s approach to security and economic stability, which he credited with rescuing the economy from collapse. ‎ ‎The governor described wasting political opportunities as a high-stakes mistake with significant long-term consequences. He stressed that solidarity with the Tinubu government was a means of securing future political influence in 2027. ‎ ‎For his part, the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Benjamin Kalu, advocated a shift from sentimental politics to strategic cooperation to drive development in Anambra State and the wider South-East. ‎ ‎He argued that the success of Igbo people in business and commerce stems from strategic thinking rather than sentiment. ‎ ‎He suggested that political progress requires moving away from protest-based approaches and focusing instead on strategic alliances. item.title: Africa Records 71.4bn Transactions, $1.8trn Instant Payments In 2025 — Report
item.description: Africa’s instant payment systems processed 71.4 billion transactions worth $1.8 trillion in 2025, nearly three times the volume recorded in 2021, according to a new report by the AfricaNenda Foundation, the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa and the World Bank Group. The fifth edition of the State of Inclusive Instant Payment Systems in Africa (SIIPS) report, published on Thursday, highlighted the rapid expansion of digital payment infrastructure across the continent but warns that access alone has not translated into widespread everyday usage. According to the report, 89 per cent of African adults live in countries with access to an instant payment system. However, a survey of 1,403 digital payment users across 15 markets found that 55 per cent still use cash for about half of their transactions. It also found that more than half of respondents had experienced payment problems, including delays and transfers to the wrong recipients, while one in three affected users never reported such incidents, largely because they did not know how to do so. “Five years ago, our first report mapped 29 instant payment systems; today there are 39, and one in two African adults live in a country served by an inclusive instant payment system IIPS,” said Sabine F. Mensah, who is Deputy CEO of AfricaNenda Foundation and lead author of the report. “The question has changed. It is no longer whether Africans can pay instantly, but whether they trust the system enough to stop reaching for cash. Our research shows that trust is won in seconds, through a payment that goes through instantly, with preventive safeguards such as recipient name validation, and a payment confirmation message received in real time. It is kept by getting timely resolution and people’s money back when something goes wrong.” (L-R): Deputy CEO AfricaNenda Foundation, Sabine Mensah; CEO AfricaNenda Foundation, Robert Ochola; and Deputy CEO AfricaNenda Foundation, Akinwale Goodluck, at the report launch on Thursday, November 19, 2026. 39 Instant Payment Systems The report identified 39 live instant payment systems across Africa, comprising 35 domestic systems in 29 countries and four regional systems. Overall, 43 African countries now have access to instant payment capabilities through domestic or regional platforms. Four domestic systems were introduced in the past year in Liberia, Burundi, Guinea and Mauritania, while a new regional system now serves the eight countries of the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU). Another 17 countries have instant payment system projects underway. Transaction volumes, according to the report, have grown by an average of 28 per cent annually since 2021, while the average transaction value has declined from $45 to $26, indicating increased use for smaller, everyday purchases. item.title: Global Securities Watchdog Warns of Quantum Computing Threat to Blockchains and Finance
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Global Securities Watchdog Warns of Quantum Computing Threat to Blockchains and Finance The International Organization of Securities Commissions, the global body for securities regulators, published a 63-page report on Thursday warning that quantum computing is a “significant medium to long-term cybersecurity challenge” for financial markets, and that moving blockchains to quantum-resistant cryptography may be especially hard. IOSCO said no practical quantum computer capable of compromising widely used cryptography exists today. “The scale and duration of the transition mean the financial sector should start preparing today,” said Jean-Paul Servais, chair of the IOSCO board, in the release. The final report drew on a survey of IOSCO members and interviews with industry experts and market participants. The group found that preparedness across the financial sector remains at an early stage. Most firms are still raising awareness, setting up governance and taking inventory of the cryptography they use, while migration testing and rollout are limited. Firms cited reliance on third parties, interoperability, limited expertise and unclear timelines as common obstacles. Why blockchains face a harder quantum migration IOSCO said the problem is sharper for public blockchains because cryptography is built into their core design. Replacing it requires hard forks and coordinated action across thousands of independent validators and node operators, and decentralized networks have no way to force a fast upgrade. The report said that could make any migration “slow and fragmented.” The report also flagged the cost of the new cryptography. It said signatures from ML-DSA-44, a post-quantum standard from the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, run about 2,420 bytes, roughly 35 to 40 times larger than the 64-byte signatures common today. That could strain throughput, storage and fees. IOSCO cited testing on Solana’s quantum-resistant testnet that showed throughput falling by about 90%. On exposed coins, the report said a capable attacker could derive private keys from public keys that are already visible on a network, and that uneven migration could leave those assets vulnerable. It singled out dormant or abandoned assets tied to exposed keys, which may be hard to move if the holders cannot be identified or cannot act. IOSCO did not mention bitcoin by name. The report’s blockchain examples were Ethereum, Solana and Tron. How soon could the threat arrive? Timing remains uncertain. IOSCO said conservative estimates put computers capable of breaking today’s cryptography in the 2030–2035 window, but several industry participants argued firms should prepare for the possibility that such machines emerge within the next five years , potentially sped up by artificial intelligence. The report also warned of “harvest now, decrypt later” attacks, in which data collected today is unlocked later. The report stopped short of setting rules. It urg

item.title: Russian national accused of stalking San Francisco techie in plot against US defense-tech giant
item.description: A Russian national is being held in custody after being arrested for allegedly spying on a US defense tech company in Palo Alto, shoulder-surfing employees, and dropping remote surveillance devices at their homes. Igor D'iu was indicted after FBI agents surveilled his activities between June and October 2026, which they say were issued as "tasks" from what is thought to be Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB), according to an affidavit [PDF] signed by an FBI special agent. After FBI agents secured a warrant to raid D'iu's temporary premises in October, they say that Telegram messages harvested from his seized devices confirmed investigators' findings and revealed that he was spying on an unnamed company. Court documents describe the company in question as a large technology and defense company with offices in Palo Alto, and media-reported links to the Russia-Ukraine war. While unconfirmed officially, the company has widely been reported as Palantir , which did not respond to our request for confirmation. D'iu allegedly received instructions from Telegram contacts, whom he only suspected were representatives of the Russian government, weeks after entering the US illegally in July. The indictment alleges he was ordered to surveil employees' homes, take photographs of their screens while working remotely at coffee shops, and permit his handlers to remotely access his laptop for the purpose of capturing data from nearby devices owned by the company’s employees. In some cases, the filing alleges, D’iu was asked to leave a laptop outside one employee's apartment complex, all while allowing his Telegram handlers to remotely operate the device. The first time, he was asked to leave the laptop for one hour while the handlers worked, and another time, he was told to drop it off in the middle of the night and only come back to collect it three hours later, the filing claims. D'iu is also allegedly to have followed two female employees in his rented car, driving dangerously and violating multiple road laws to do so. One of the two employees was followed briefly, but D'iu followed another for nearly 30 miles, according to the affidavit signed by FBI special agent Winston Wong. D'iu was said to have followed the woman as she performed U-turns, illegal left turns, ran red lights, navigated via back and side streets, and through grocery store parking lots. The car following her only peeled away after the woman drove to the San Francisco Mission police station on the advice of a 911 call handler. Questioned about the incident, which according to police reports caused the woman significant emotional distress, D'iu confirmed he was the driver but claimed he was following her to ask her out on a date. item.title: Netflix's '3 Body Problem' season 2 trailer gives us a release date and a chilling warning: 'They are coming to exterminate us'
item.description: null " 3 Body Problem ," Netflix's unsettling adaptation of the first book in Chinese author Cixin Liu's epic alien invasion trilogy, "Remembrance of Earth’s Past," made a serious impact on viewers searching for hardcore E.T. drama and now an explosive new trailer for season 2 has just entered our orbit. This sensational saga about a malevolent interstellar society trying to exist within the unpredictable orbital mechanics of a planet and its triple sun system that forms an Earth-bound armada still has us a bit slack-jawed more than two years after debuting in 2024 . Now we're admittedly eager for this shortened 6-episode sophomore outing, which is officially arriving on Jan. 14, 2027. Delivered by Emmy Award-winning "Game of Thrones" team of David Benioff and D.B. Weiss and "True Blood's" Alexander Woo, "3 Body Problem" season 2 revolves around the combined forces of the Planetary Defense Council as they mount a daring deep space counterattack against the San-Ti. The San-Ti have arrived in Netflix's "3 Body Problem" season 2! (Image credit: Netflix) These Trisolarians are not the friendliest of galactic neighbors, and prior to the all-out invasion their primary goal was to thwart humanity’s ability to create advanced defense weaponry in the four centuries it would take for them to enter our solar system. This time it's more about the next phase of ultimate survival and dire actions taken by anti-alien and pro-alien factions. Season 2 leaps forward 400 years and focuses on the results of the Wallfacer Project, a secret initiative where chosen individuals worked on solutions in isolation as to not attract the attention of the Trisolarian's omnipresent AI surveillance technology called sophons. While the debut season was based on Liu's Hugo Award-winning 2008 novel, "The Three-Body Problem," this upcoming Netflix offering will adapt the second book, "The Dark Forest." 2010's "Death's End" closed out the acclaimed sci-fi trilogy. Netflix Netflix Netflix Netflix "So much of season 1 is about the mystery of what's happening," co-creator and co-executive producer David Benioff tells Netflix. "By the time season 2 starts, we have a lot more information. We know there is a hostile alien civilization out there, the San-Ti, and they’re coming our way, and they want our planet for themselves." Landing on Jan. 14, 2027, "3 Body Problem" season 2's international cast includes returners Jess Hong, Benedict Wong, Jovan Adepo, Eiza González, Liam Cunningham, Marlo Kelly, Sea Shimooka, Saamer Usmani, Alex Sharp and Josh Brener. Joining them are fresh cast members Claudia Doumit, Ellie de Lange, Alfie Allen, David Yip and Jordan Sunshine. Watch 3 Body Problem on Netflix: Standard with ads: $8.99/month Standard: $19.99/month Premium (4K): $26.99/month

item.title: ICJ ruling on Myanmar genocide: ‘Historic victory for Rohingya, landmark for international justice’
item.description: Erin Ogunkeye welcomes Reed Brody, Member of the International Commission of Jurists, Human Rights Lawyer and veteran war crimes prosecutor. The International Court of Justice's ruling on Myanmar marks, according to Brody, "a historic victory for the Rohingya, but also a landmark for international justice." He explains how the court assessed evidence of genocidal intent, rejecting Myanmar's justification of its military operations as counterterrorism. He argues that "the existence of an armed conflict or a security objective doesn't exclude genocidal intent," a finding he believes will have "far-reaching implications in future genocide cases," including South Africa's case against Israel over Gaza. Brody also discusses the Gambia's role in bringing the case and growing challenges to international accountability, warning that "we're in a very dangerous moment."

item.title: Xi demonstrating China's 'global status', occupying 'central position' in relation to Trump & Putin
item.description: Sharon Gaffney is pleased to welcome Rex Li, professor of international relations at King's College London. For Professor Li, the meeting between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin in China is less about "reaching concrete agreements and a common position." Rather, he argues, it is about demonstrating Xi's ability to bring the American and Russian leaders together to discuss major geopolitical issues. Li believes that Xi Jinping has the most to gain from the meeting, as it allows him to demonstrate China's global status and its role as a diplomatic convener. Putin may also benefit from the opportunity to meet the two leaders despite Russia's international isolation following its invasion of Ukraine.

item.title: Europe's biggest gas supplier battling cyberattack – with no timeline for recovery
item.description: Norwegian energy giant Equinor is battling a cyberattack on its IT systems, though the company insists that hackers haven't disrupted its oil and gas production. Equinor, Europe's largest supplier of natural gas, first disclosed the attack on Tuesday evening, saying it had called in the relevant resources to deal with the intrusion and had found no indication that any data had been stolen. In an update on Wednesday, the company said it had a better handle on how the attack was carried out and which of its systems had been compromised, though it stopped short of sharing either of those details. "As this is not a virus attack, there is no risk of the attack spreading," Equinor said. The company added that it had found nothing to suggest the incident would affect employees, partners, or suppliers. In a further update on Thursday, Equinor said the attack remained ongoing but did not appear to be specifically targeting the company. Production continued normally, with no indications that data had been stolen or altered. The incident has been reported to police. What kind of attack Equinor is dealing with remains a mystery. The company hasn't identified those responsible, disclosed whether it's received any demands from the hackers, or said when it expects the affected systems to be fully restored. The Register has asked Equinor to elaborate, including whether any of its UK operations have been affected and whether the hackers managed to venture beyond its corporate IT network. Equinor spokesperson Ellen Maria Skjelsbæk told Norwegian news agency NTB that the company hadn't lost access to its IT systems, though staff could have trouble accessing some corporate applications and services. Email appears to be among the casualties, with Reuters reporting that the company's internal email system was down. Equinor, which traded as Statoil until 2018, is still largely in the hands of the Norwegian state, which owns 67 percent of the company. The oil and gas biz employs around 25,000 people and operates in more than 20 countries. The bulk of Equinor's oil and gas production takes place off the coast of Norway, but the company also pumps oil and gas in the UK, US, Brazil, and Canada. It's one of the companies behind Dogger Bank, the enormous offshore wind project off England's northeast coast, and is also in the business of capturing and storing carbon dioxide. Equinor's assurances about production will be particularly welcome in Europe, which has become increasingly reliant on Norwegian gas since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. The attack comes just weeks after Norway's National Security Authority (NSM) raised its cyberattack risk assessment to four on a five-point scale . The agency said the number of successful cyber operations against Norwegian businesses had tripled over the preceding six months and warned of potential disruption to essential services, including water and electricity supplies. item.title: [VIDEO] Drama As Ngige Urges Residents To Vote For APC ‘From Top To Bottom’ At Anambra Presidential Rally
item.description: There was a mild drama at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Anambra State on Thursday when a former governor of the state, Chris Ngige, urged residents to vote for the APC in the 2027 presidential, National Assembly, and House of Assembly elections. The former Minister of Labour and Employment, who spoke in Igbo, said Anambra residents had one target. “We will vote for the APC from top to bottom,” Ngige said, prompting reactions from participants at the rally, including Governor Charles Soludo of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), who stood beside him on stage and told his predecessor that the rally is a joint one. The former governor, who said he was not surprised by the reactions, later told members of APGA to vote for candidates of their choice. “Okay, members of APGA — freedom of choice — when you get to the polling booth, vote for the better place,” he said. Ngige added that while people were free to choose between APGA and the APC, Anambra desires to be connected to the Federal Government at the centre and get it through the ruling party. Earlier, the former minister said he remains a member of the APC, claiming that he brought the party to the South-East. “I am still a member of the APC, bona fide member, because I brought APC to the South East — 2013/2014,” he said. “The only thing is that I told people I am on sabbatical, but even if I am on sabbatical, my governor cannot be doing something, and the Vice President is coming physically, and the governor has called me to say we are here, and I would say I won’t come. No.” Ngige said people should not be forced but persuaded to vote during the 2027 general election. He also said those stopping people from campaigning are not doing so in the name of the APC. “We don’t want that — destruction of vehicles, stoning of people. No! We don’t want that. We must emulate other people practising democracy,” the former Anambra governor said. “Democracy gives you the right of choice; even inside the same family, you must exercise that.” Watch Ngige’s remarks in the video below. ﻿ The post [VIDEO] Drama As Ngige Urges Residents To Vote For APC ‘From Top To Bottom’ At Anambra Presidential Rally appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: NASA Science Data Powers New Method to Discover Hard-to-Find Pulsars
item.description: 5 min read NASA Science Data Powers New Method to Discover Hard-to-Find Pulsars NASA’s Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope, illustrated here, scans the entire sky every three hours as it orbits Earth. Its publicly available data helps scientists find the rapidly spinning cores of dead stars, known as pulsars. NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center/Chris Smith (USRA/GESTAR) An international team of scientists has developed a method that can find pulsars in publicly available NASA data about a million times faster than before. This opens the door to discovering many more of these rapidly spinning objects. A paper describing the results published Thursday in the Physical Review Letters. Using 15 years of data from NASA’s Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope and a cryptography-based method developed by study co-authors Dotan Gazith and Barak Zackay from the Weizmann Institute of Science in Israel, the team found PSR J1622−7204, an isolated pulsar spinning 261 times per second, using the equivalent of 10 hours of computing time on a standard computer processor. By comparison, the previous best method failed to find the pulsar, despite using enough computing power that a standard processor would take 600 years to perform the calculation. A pulsar is a rapidly spinning neutron star that sweeps beams of radiation toward Earth, much like a lighthouse. Finding pulsars in gamma-ray data is extraordinarily difficult because Fermi detects only a tiny number of photons from a given pulsar, mixed in with background noise from other gamma-ray-emitting sources and the broader universe. To find the signal, researchers must accurately guess several unknowns at once: how fast the star spins, how quickly the spin is slowing down, and precisely where it sits in the sky. Searching every possible combination would require an impossible number of computations. “We don’t see every rotation from the pulsar, and we can’t just count the rotations to work out where the photon came from,” said lead author Daniel Pook-Kolb, a scientist at the Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics (Albert Einstein Institute) in Germany. “We have a four-dimensional grid, and we must search each direction with millions of trials in it. There’s just not enough computing power on Earth to do it.” This artist’s concept shows a pulsar, which emits light in regular pulses as it rotates, like a cosmic lighthouse. Pulsars are dense remnants of exploded stars, and are part of a class of objects called neutron stars. Openly available data from NASA’s Fermi space telescope can help scientists spot pulsars in the gamma-ray spectrum. NASA/JPL-Caltech Traditionally, scientists have searched for these pulsars by breaking Fermi data into smaller chunks and analyzing them by crowdsourcing computing power from volunteers around the world. item.title: Ledger Finds Tampered Hardware Wallets in Berlin, Probes Two in Dubai
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Ledger Finds Tampered Hardware Wallets in Berlin, Probes Two in Dubai Ledger has confirmed tampered hardware wallets in Berlin and is investigating two more in Dubai, the wallet maker said Wednesday, widening a probe into spy implants it first traced to resellers in Southeast Asia in October. The new cases are “the same incident,” Ledger said in an update on its support site. Every device it has confirmed carries the same physical modification, built to capture a user’s recovery phrase while the wallet is being set up. “There is no flaw in Ledger’s secure chip or operating system, and no confirmed case involving a device bought on ledger.com,” the company wrote on X. Ledger also found one affected Nano Gen5, its newer model, among the Southeast Asian resellers it had already paused. It did not give a count for Berlin, describing the cases there only as “a few tampered units.” Berlin buyers told to check in Ledger asked anyone who bought one of its devices in Berlin since January 2026 to contact its support team. In Dubai, the company said it is working with distribution partners to learn how the two suspected units entered circulation. Its Donjon security team is examining suspected devices, and resellers have been asked to pause sales wherever inspections are still running. Customers who are worried about a device should stop using it and should not open it themselves, Ledger said. Its advice is to move funds to a new wallet created on a device bought directly from ledger.com, without reusing the old recovery phrase or passphrase, because a tampered unit can capture both. The company also told affected users to file a report with local authorities. For a limited time, Ledger is offering physical inspections, including X-rays, at its factory in Vierzon, France. “This continues to be a small number of devices overall, and we do expect more to be discovered in our investigation and via social media,” Ledger said. How the implant works The probe began in October, after users in Southeast Asia reported drained wallets. Ledger linked the cases to devices sold through CryptoBilis, a Malaysia-based authorized reseller, and asked it to stop selling and shipping Ledger products, BleepingComputer reported . In an Oct. 15 blog post , Ledger said a “highly organized criminal group” spent months buying genuine devices, fitting them with hidden components and slipping them back into distribution through resellers. “They were patient, they spent millions, and they struck in one coordinated operation, draining wallets,” the company wrote. Researchers who opened tampered units found a small chip, an eSIM and a cellular module hidden inside the case. The implant read the 24-word recovery phrase off the screen during setup and sent it out over a mobile network. Ledger’s Genuine Check cannot detect an added implant when the original secure chip is intact, the report said. That is how Ledger can say its chip is sound and still have a problem. Anyone

item.title: European Commission scrambles to contain AI-assisted cyberattack
item.description: The European Commission is picking up the pieces after hackers wielding an AI-powered security testing tool targeted its internal IT systems, potentially exposing staff members' personal data. The attack, first reported by Politico, has caused more than 10 days of disruption at the EU's executive arm. Among the applications temporarily taken offline were Sysper, which staff use to access payslips, submit timesheets, and request vacation time, and MyPMO, which handles medical reimbursements. Both were brought back online earlier this week, though Sysper fell over again on Wednesday. The Commission's translation services were also affected. "The European Commission has taken the necessary steps in response to a detected cyber campaign," Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier told Politico. "Individual systems were targeted and, in line with our standard practice, we have informed those concerned." According to Politico's sources, the Commission's cybersecurity defenders detected hackers using ARTEX, a publicly available AI-powered penetration testing framework. The incident prompted an emergency meeting of the Commission's Corporate Management Board earlier this month, and tech commissioner Henna Virkkunen briefed her fellow commissioners on Wednesday. The Commission has yet to respond to The Register 's questions about the attack, including whether the crooks got their hands on employee data or whether the applications were simply taken offline as a precaution. The attack might not come as much of a surprise to the Commission's own security bods. CERT-EU, which looks after the cybersecurity of EU institutions, warned on November 5 that it had spotted what it believed to be ARTEX-assisted attacks against organizations under its watch. The developer behind ARTEX pulled the project's GitHub repository in October after reports that hackers were putting the software to use. But by then, the code was out in the wild, and anyone wanting to have a crack at an organization's IT estate could get hold of one of several forks. The FBI also sounded the alarm last week [PDF], revealing that researchers had found more than 1,600 ARTEX consoles exposed to the internet. In some of the attacks detailed by the Feds, hackers went from identifying a target to obtaining privileged access in less than three hours. “What used to take a skilled operator days or weeks of chaining is now happening in hours because frameworks like ARTEX let a single actor stand up fleets of agents that plan, probe, exploit, and move laterally with almost no further human input after the initial goal is set,” Snehal Antani, CEO of security firm Horizon3.ai, told The Register. Antani said the proliferation of these tools could also make life harder for investigators trying to establish who's behind an attack, as government-backed hackers and garden-variety cybercriminals increasingly draw from the same toolbox. Commission staff at least appear to have been paid on time. According to Politico,

item.title: Empire State Building glows gold for NASA's Voyager spacecraft | Space photo of the day for Nov. 19, 2026
item.description: null The Empire State Building is illuminated in gold to celebrate Voyager 1 hitting one light-day from Earth, seen here on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026, from SUMMIT One Vanderbilt in New York City. (Image credit: NASA/Bill Ingalls) The Empire State Building glowed in glittering gold last night (Nov. 17) to celebrate NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft hitting one light-day from Earth. And it isn't the only building celebrating this achievement with a sparkling display. What is it? Today (Nov. 18) at 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT), NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft hit one light-day from Earth. About 16 billion miles (about 26 billion kilometers) away, this is the point at which it takes a full day (or 24 hours) for one light particle to get from us to the probe. So any signal we send to Voyager 1 or it sends back now takes a full day as the spacecraft continues to explore interstellar space. To celebrate the major milestone for the farthest human-made object in history, the Empire State Building in New York City lit up in gold . This golden glow references the Golden Record onboard both the Voyager 1 and 2 spacecraft. And the Empire State Building wasn't the only major landmark to celebrate the occasion. The Space Needle in Seattle, Washington, and both the Willis Tower and the Skydeck Chicago in Chicago, Illinois have all been illuminated gold to mark the milestone. Why is it incredible? The Golden Record that these gold glowing buildings are referencing serves as an inanimate ambassador for Earth , carrying information about humanity, our planet, the other species who live here, the languages we speak, the music we listen to and so much more. It even includes instructions for building a record player to play the record. The Voyager mission has, and continues to, make incredible scientific discoveries and observations throughout our solar system and now in interstellar space. But this Golden Record provides an additional aspect to the mission that connects us here on Earth to whatever unknown life may exist out there. If some sort of life forms out in the cosmos were to ever come across Voyager and its Golden Record at any point in the distant future, they might learn a little bit about our small blue dot.

item.title: How Silicon Valley lost the public, with Crooked Media’s Jon Favreau
item.description: Today, I’m talking with Jon Favreau, a political commentator and cofounder of Crooked Media. You probably know Jon best from a little show called Pod Save America , which Jon started with a group of fellow Obama staffers in the wake of Donald Trump’s election in 2016. It’s now one of the most popular podcasts in the country. Since then, Pod Save America and the company created around it, Crooked, have become one of the major success stories of independent liberal media. So one of my central questions for Jon was why he thought Democrats swept the midterms earlier this month and, more importantly, why it happened now — especially after a wave of tech billionaires made big swings to the right while buying huge pillars of the information ecosystem. That’s Elon Musk buying Twitter and turning it into X, Mark Zuckerberg sucking up to Trump while tearing down Meta’s content moderation infrastructure, the Ellison family buying stakes in TikTok, turning over the leadership of CBS News and now potentially CNN while integrating Warner into Skydance… the list goes on. How did they all miss the huge swing in the mood of the public — or, more apocalyptically, fail in their attempts to control the media and thus influence the public? Verge subscribers, don’t forget you get exclusive access to ad-free Decoder wherever you get your podcasts. Head here . Not a subscriber? You can sign up here . Crooked itself is also just a fascinating business, as all creator businesses are. When we think of what you might call news creators, we tend to look to the right — after all, conservative media have been building an alternative, direct-to-consumer pipeline since the dawn of talk radio. But Jon and his fellow Crooked cofounders created a reliable template for liberal creators, and it’s working. Crooked hired its first CEO a few years ago, now offers more than a dozen original shows, and has a staff of around 100 people working on everything from live events to political advocacy. Jon tells me the subscription business has crossed 65,000 members. So of course I wanted to know how Jon feels about topics we cover a lot here on Decoder : online distribution, the platform power of YouTube, and how you balance running a media business that has to make money with a newsroom that, ultimately, has a political mission and a strong point of view. Of course, AI. Jon has turned his own podcast Offline into something close to an AI policy show this year. He has a lot of thoughts on how Congress should tackle the issue. Before we get going, do me a favor and subscribe to Decoder on YouTube, where we put out new episodes every Monday and Thursday.
